diagnosis: kernel_check_invariants aborted with 'falsified binary clause escaped propagation' — a missed unit propagation at a claimed fixpoint. Root cause: decide_guard did not require a propagation fixpoint, so under a free N1 schedule the random policy could DECIDE on an un-propagated trail. This kernel assigns a forced literal at the CURRENT decision level (not its true level, kissat assign.c/backtrack.c), so a decision taken before propagation completes lets the pending implications be assigned one level too deep (and a later backtrack can then drop them); a binary conflict escaped. Sound in the abstract DPLL calculus (any interleaving of Decide/UnitPropagate is sound; levels are derived there) — the fixpoint precondition is imposed by the current-level assignment scheme, not by logic. Never reachable in DefaultPolicy (it propagates to fixpoint before deciding, the universal BCP-then-branch discipline); exposed by V2 Backbone's high root-unit yield, which makes the un-propagated-then-decide state common under the random policy. Fixed 2026-07-16: decide_guard now requires propagate_head == trail.size. The invariant this restores: a STATE-ADVANCING rule (Decide + all inprocessing) may only run at a propagation fixpoint; only Propagate (and Analyze/Backjump on a recorded conflict) are exempt. Also strengthened kernel_check_invariants to flag missed UNITS (binary + large), not only escaped conflicts, so the whole class is caught eagerly. The deeper relaxation (true-level assignment + chronological backtracking, CaDiCaL) that would remove the precondition stays the §5.4 kernel candidate first filed from corpus 002.
